# ★ CORRECTION LOGGED 2026-07-31 — I TOLD WILL THIS SURFACE MIGHT BE "STRUCTURALLY UNOBSERVABLE." THAT WAS WRONG, AND THE ERROR WAS MINE, NOT THE MARKET'S.

#   That claim was asserted off a search set of ONE outlet (The Insurer). A scope-negative — "it is absent / unobservable / undefined" — is the claim that stops anyone else looking, so it needs the counterparty standard, and it did not get it (auto-memory `finding_scope_negative_needs_the_counterparty_standard`).

#   The corrected diagnosis: Black Sea AWRP is a privately-negotiated PER-VOYAGE number that reaches print only when a journalist canvasses brokers — i.e. it is EVENT-DRIVEN OBSERVABLE, not continuously observable. Between step-changes there is genuinely nothing to print, so the absence rows below are CORRECT. But prints DO occur on step-changes, and a one-outlet watch will miss them.

#   ⚠️ WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION: the 7/24-7/31 no-print finding HOLDS — it has now been re-tested against EIGHT outlets (below) rather than one, including two dated INSIDE the gap window (Insurance Journal 7/24, Kpler) which were fetched in full and carry NO rate figure. The finding got stronger; the diagnosis got replaced.

#   INSTITUTIONAL/BROKER: S&P Global Platts (assesses Black Sea AWRP with port-level granularity) · Marsh (name the individual: Dylan Mortimer = Marine Hull UK War Leader, quoted on BLACK SEA; Marcus Baker is the Gulf/Hormuz voice FALCON uses — do not cross them)
#   RELAY/SECONDARY (usable for discovery, NEVER as the print): Cyprus Shipping News · beinsure · Ship Universe · Maritime Executive · ofimagazine
#   ⚠️ ALWAYS date-verify: this beat recirculates hard. 8 vintage traps caught to date, most recently the Dec-2025 baseline (RU 0.65-0.8% / UA 0.5%) resurfacing as if fresh in 7/31 searches.
# 🎯 CONTINUOUS PROXY REGISTERED 2026-07-31 — THE REAL FIX FOR AN EVENT-DRIVEN INSTRUMENT:

#   BALTIC EXCHANGE ROUTE **TD6 = 135,000 mt CPC -> Augusta.** That is LITERALLY the route through the terminal this desk tracks, and it is assessed DAILY and reported weekly in free trade press (IndexBox, The DCN, Baltic Exchange weekly roundup).

#   War-risk cost is EMBEDDED in the freight a charterer pays, so TD6 moves continuously where the AWRP moves discretely. It does NOT isolate the war-risk component — freight also carries tightness, tonnage availability and voyage economics — so TD6 is a CONTINUOUS PROXY, never a substitute for a rate print.

#   ⚠️ USE IT AS A TRIPWIRE, NOT A LEVEL: a large TD6 move with no AWRP print is the cue to go canvass the 8 outlets above, i.e. it tells you WHEN to look for a print you would otherwise miss. That is precisely the gap that let 7/24-7/31 pass unexamined.
# UNIT DISCIPLINE: all premia are % OF HULL VALUE per voyage unless the Unit column says otherwise. Do not compare across ports/legs without checking Unit and Scope.
